raw.rationale: The presence of intravascular atypical cells on skin biopsy, as shown by hematoxylin-eosin stained sections and CD56 immunostaining, is a key diagnostic feature of intravascular large B-cell lymphoma. The patient's symptoms, including fever, hypotension, and a new skin eruption, along with laboratory findings such as anemia (low hemoglobin level) and thrombocytopenia (low platelet count), also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The skin biopsy findings and clinical presentation do not specifically suggest Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, which typically presents with different skin manifestations and often has a more chronic course.

rejected.label: Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm
rejected.why: While this condition can present with skin involvement, the specific biopsy findings and clinical context provided do not align closely with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and biopsy findings do not specifically suggest Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma, which is often associated with HTLV-1 infection and has distinct clinical and laboratory features.

rejected.label: Pembrolizumab-induced Immune-mediated Dermatitis
rejected.why: Although the patient has a history of a morbilliform reaction to pembrolizumab, the new skin eruption's characteristics and the presence of intravascular atypical cells on biopsy suggest a more serious underlying condition rather than a dermatitis reaction.

transplant_cands: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms
